historical_references.reference: The Puranic legend describes Kran as the king of the serpents and a great devotee of Lord Vishnu. He is also known as Anantha, Vasuki, and Shesha. Kran is considered to be the protector of the universe and is often depicted as coiling around the cosmic ocean. He is also believed to be the king of the underworld, and his common epithet, 'Kala', signifies time.

Another reference to Kran is found in the Mahabharata, where he is mentioned as the king of the serpents and the one who assumes the form of the demon Kaliya to torment the Yadavas. Kran is also the one who later saves the Yadavas by slaying Kaliya and is hailed as a hero by them.
